title: The law of sines over the constructed reals, as |U x V| = ||U|| ||V|| sin, with the cross product identified with the existing triangle determinant
statement: For two points (vectors) U, V of the plane CPoint over the constructed (Bishop) reals, with k and h : PosBound (||U|| ||V||) k, |U x V| ~ ||U|| ||V|| sinAngle(U,V), where |.| is CReal.abs, U x V is CPoint.crossV, and ~ is CReal.Equiv. Separately and definitionally, CPoint.cross_eq_crossV proves cross A B C ~ crossV (sub B A) (sub C B) BY equiv_refl: the three-point triangle determinant the library already had IS the two-vector cross product at the two edge vectors. So the left side is twice the area of the triangle, and this is also the (1/2) a b sin C area formula.

formal.statement: theorem CPoint.law_of_sines : ((x0 : CPoint) -> ((x1 : CPoint) -> ((x2 : AxNat) -> ((x3 : CReal.PosBound (CReal.mul (CPoint.norm x0) (CPoint.norm x1)) x2) -> CReal.Equiv (CReal.abs (CPoint.crossV x0 x1)) (CReal.mul (CReal.mul (CPoint.norm x0) (CPoint.norm x1)) (CPoint.sinAngle x0 x1 x2 x3))))))

evidence.supports: `CPoint.law_of_sines` and `CPoint.cross_eq_crossV` are admitted with exactly the types their statement pins record, with empty axiom footprints. `new_definitions_have_the_intended_value` additionally pins `crossV`'s VALUE at a symbolic argument and asserts it still contains a `CReal.neg`, because the kernel cannot tell you a definition is wrong -- a symmetric `crossV` would type-check and would make this statement false.

provenance.established_by: lane angles-and-isometries (2026-09-04), roadmap W1-8/W2-13, ADR-1615. Kernel theorems over CReal (the constructed Bishop reals, ADR-0512) in crates/axeyum-lean-kernel/src/creal_point/angle.rs and creal_point/isometry.rs, all admitted through Kernel::add_declaration with an empty axiom_footprint.

prior_art.who: Nasir al-Din al-Tusi and earlier Indian and Islamic authors
prior_art.what: the law of sines for plane triangles
prior_art.attribution: standard attribution; this lane did not consult the primary source.

notes:
WHAT IS NOT PROVED. The ratio form a/sin A = b/sin B = c/sin C is NOT proved. This is the product form for one pair of vectors; deriving the ratio form needs the PosBound producer described in F:pythagorean-identity-for-the-plane-angle's notes (so the three angles of one triangle can each be formed) plus a circumradius identity. Recording this fact under the name 'law of sines' without this paragraph would let a reader infer the ratio form.

sinAngle is UNSIGNED, so the left side carries an absolute value and the statement says nothing about orientation. A signed version would need a decision on the sign of a real.

Constructive: no Classical.em, no propext, no funext, no Quot.sound.
